story.value: Erbium's name comes from the Swedish town of Ytterby, where the ore gadolinite, in which erbium was found, was first mined.
Erbium was discovered in 1843 by Carl-Gustav Mosander, a Swedish surgeon and chemist, in a sample of yttrium.
Scientists soon confused the substances erbia and terbia, and by 1877 they had reversed their names.

uses.value: Erbium is added to fiber optic cables, where it is used as a signal amplifier.
Erbia, a pink compound of erbium, is used to color glass and glazes.
Erbium is alloyed with vanadium to make it softer and easier to shape.
